Expression-bodied async arrows also enter the same CFG through a normalized return block, eliminating their distinct settled-await ordering path.
- Value-producing conditional expressions with suspension now lower as recursive generic async CFG branches rather than eager flat await lists or conditional-specific continuation templates. Each selected arm independently feeds declaration initialization, identifier assignment, value-discarding expression completion, return/throw completion, nested conditional values, or switch dispatch; synchronous and awaited arms compose, selector exceptions follow the state's exception edge, and unselected arm side effects never run. Return routes use the async function's resolved contextual type when choosing array/object literal storage—including catch returns—without casting away a returned Promise or suppressing thenable adoption. Tests: `async_await_conditional_value_cfg`, `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_return_two_await`, `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_mixed_sync_await`, `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_throwing_selector`, `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_mixed_structural_sync_await`, `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_mixed_dynamic_promise`.
- Embedded-await `if`, `while`, `do...while`, and ordinary `for` conditions plus `switch` discriminants now finish through typed expression-completion branch/dispatch edges in the generic async CFG. Bare awaited conditions apply central JavaScript truthiness to any supported fulfilled type, including empty/nonempty strings, rather than requiring boolean or testing a C pointer. Reconstructed arithmetic/comparison conditions and discriminants reuse rooted expression slots, while conditional and arbitrary-cardinality logical conditions use an explicit graph of synchronous/awaited leaves with truthy, falsy, and nullish successors. Mixed operands such as `sync() && await source` and `await source && sync()` therefore retain side-effect order and skip the unselected side. Await sources may contain callback closures; capture discovery traverses those closures and carries callback-only outer bindings as shared cells. Routing adds no Promise job and preserves unchosen ternary branches plus `&&`/`||`/`??` source skipping. Tests: `async_await_expression_condition_cfg`, `async_await_do_body_multi_condition_continue`, `async_await_do_body_conditional_condition_continue`.
- Await-bearing multi-declarator variable statements now normalize into ordered single-declarator async CFG states while preserving declaration flags and left-to-right initialization. This removes the legacy nested-`for` initializer path for awaited `var` lists across direct, selector-chain, recursive-selector, awaited-condition, and awaited-incrementor graphs. Await-free labeled `for...of` / `for...in` states may also remain atomic when every labeled completion is proven local to that iterator loop, allowing complex outer awaited loop control to use the same CFG without admitting escaping labels. Tests: `async_await_post_await_if_await_condition_nested_awaited_var_for_initializer`, `async_await_post_await_if_await_condition_nested_awaited_var_for_loop_control`.
- Generic async CFG admission now permits nested callback closures inside an awaited source expression when the surrounding statement graph is otherwise supported. The callback captures the CFG's shared binding cell rather than a transient continuation frame, so rebinding performed by a pending Promise executor remains visible after one or more suspensions in GC and no-GC builds. Test: `async_closure_direct_await_capture`.
- Embedded-await `return` and `throw` expressions now finish through typed async CFG completion states instead of invoking inline early-return emitters inside a `void` callback. Staged values route through catch and awaited-finally edges, return expressions retain the function's awaited contextual type while reconstructing nested arrays/objects, and typed aggregate Promise results no longer cross the ABI as mismatched dynamic storage. Tests: `async_await_expression_completion_cfg`, `async_await_branch_block_five_await_expression_fallthrough`, `async_await_branch_block_structural_expression_fallthrough`.
- Generic async CFG planning now prunes states unreachable through normal, exceptional, and finally-completion edges, so source after unconditional rethrow is neither emitted nor required to keep otherwise-dead declarations alive. If that worklist removes every planned suspension, its zero-suspension result remains the canonical lowering instead of falling into a synchronous emitter that must reject the original await-bearing syntax; genuinely suspension-free functions retain the direct path. The discriminated finalizer-entry model stores a normal successor only for normal completion, keeping every retained graph target closed. A compact planner property proves reachability, target closure, suspension ownership, and protected abrupt routing; the existing E2E inventory is regression evidence only.
- Generic async CFG states now retain referenced closure bindings as typed shared-cell handles, preserving mutation aliasing and dynamic-value roots across arbitrary suspension edges without retaining a pointer to an expired closure call frame. Async-iterator bindings and terminal results use that same continuation scope instead of forwarding an internal shared-cell representation as a source value.
- Nested awaited graphs now lower through a statement-level typed async CFG with explicit state IDs, successor edges, heterogeneous expression slots, per-state exception targets, and indexed finally completion regions rather than another syntax-depth template. One heap-backed program-counter continuation composes nested `while`/`do`/`for`, awaited `for` headers, direct awaited branches, synchronous/awaited switch dispatch, bare awaits, awaited declarations/assignments, terminal completion, nested `try/catch`, and every completion kind through awaited `finally`. The shared expression-sequence planner now feeds CFG states for one or more awaits embedded in arithmetic, unary expressions, templates, calls, property/element access, arrays/objects and spreads, expression statements, and `&&`/`||`/`??`; each resumed value has typed rooted storage, stable callees preserve awaited-argument ordering, and skipped short-circuit sources are never evaluated. Promise rejection, callback `longjmp`, caught recovery/rethrow, labelled exits, and cleanup overrides converge through rooted exception, pending-return Promise, and per-region completion slots. Tests: `async_await_nested_loop_cfg`, `async_await_nested_finally_cfg`, `async_await_nested_expression_cfg`.
- Lexical blocks now expose nested awaited `while`, `do...while`, and ordinary `for` conditions to the typed async loop continuation planner. Natural body fallthrough is represented as a loop-condition completion edge, arbitrary-cardinality pre-loop declarations use hygienic captured storage, await-free post-loop statements run on normal exit, rejection skips that shared tail, and settled condition re-entry queues Promise jobs instead of recursively running iterations. Label-aware `break` and `continue` edges survive suspension through the same typed completion plan; guarded fallthrough and explicit `if/else` forms retain their common body prefix, nested synchronous loops route enclosing-label exits to explicit continuation/fallthrough basic blocks, and labelled `do...while` executes its first body synchronously before any condition job. Tests: `async_await_nested_lexical_loop_graph`, `async_await_nested_lexical_labelled_loop_graph`, `async_await_nested_lexical_enclosing_label_graph`.
- Lexical blocks now expose awaited `try/finally` and `try/catch/finally` completion edges with explicit post-finally statements. The protected initial edge evaluates the synchronous try prefix and first await source under the same exception route, so prefix throws enter catch/finally immediately while fulfilled and rejected suspensions retain queued Promise ordering. Fulfilled try work runs before cleanup and the shared lexical tail, rejected try work skips the tail unless caught, and catch recovery converges through cleanup. Test: `async_await_nested_lexical_try_graph`.
- Lexical blocks now expose nested `switch` suspension graphs through the shared typed branch representation. The discriminant is evaluated exactly once; case selection, a default before later cases, fallthrough, top-level switch `break`, branch-local awaited declarations, shadowed bindings, rejection, and the shared lexical tail retain JavaScript ordering. Await-bearing control flow now terminates prelude discovery instead of being misclassified as synchronous prelude work, and await-free clause paths use a synchronous block-completion edge rather than a fabricated suspension. Test: `async_await_nested_lexical_switch_graph`.
- Lexical blocks can now expose nested `if` suspension graphs while retaining hygienic symbol-specific storage for enclosing and shadowed bindings. Unequal branches may carry an awaited declaration only on the suspending path, while a selected zero-suspension entry edge executes its branch tail, shared block tail, and typed completion synchronously instead of taking a synthetic Promise microtask. Fulfillment, rejection, fallthrough ordering, and shadowing match the JavaScript reference. Test: `async_await_nested_lexical_if_graph`.
- Synchronous `try` / `catch` / `finally` lowering now pops each exception frame on its `setjmp` landing path before entering catch/finally code or rethrowing. Throws from async continuation preludes can no longer jump back into expired callback stack frames and stall the event loop. Tests: `async_await_post_await_if_await_condition_try_catch_prelude`, `exceptions`, `promise_callback_throw`.
- Conditional suspension states now execute both their selected branch-local tail and the state graph's shared post-await completion statements. Unequal nested branches with one or more awaits therefore converge on a common terminal `throw` instead of silently resolving after the branch's final suspension. Test: `async_await_nested_conditional_unequal_terminal_throw`.
- Terminal async `if` conditions containing a direct `await` now suspend through the queued Promise continuation path for functions, methods, lifted arrows, and statically selected enclosing lexical branches. Fulfillment selects the original return branch after resumption, rejection propagates through the result Promise, and already-settled sources no longer complete synchronously ahead of earlier await-free async calls. Test: `async_await_if_condition`.
- Async statement suspension graphs now carry an await-free edge from their final suspension state to typed function completion. One or more awaits in a nested lexical block can therefore resume through shared continuation states and the original block tail, with hygienic symbol-specific storage for locals declared before or between suspensions, outer/inner name shadowing, and rejection at either suspension. Conditional branch captures sharing a source name are merged only when their storage types agree, while symbol identity continues to govern references. Test: `async_await_nested_lexical_block`.
- Async loop rejection routing now distinguishes absent catch/finally state indices from state zero, marks simple catch edges explicitly, preserves synchronous and awaited catch recovery before loop continuation, runs awaited finally cleanup after rejected try awaits, and does not invent an undefined terminal adapter for synchronous throw branches. Tests: `async_await_do_body_try_await_catch_await_continue`, `async_await_do_body_try_await_catch_continue`, `async_await_do_body_try_await_named_catch_continue`, `async_await_do_body_try_finally_await_cleanup_reject`, `async_await_do_body_await_if_sync_throw`.
- The canonical async block entry is shared across function declarations, instance/static methods, lifted arrows, captured closures, and object methods. Async iterators are consequently available to every block-bodied async function form, and closure captures used after suspension are copied into the continuation environment instead of retaining an out-of-scope closure-frame pointer.
- Async leading continuations now use collection-backed step/conditional-branch and expression-sequence representations; the numbered fixed-shape analyzers, emitters, adapters, and dispatch fallbacks were removed. Semantic regressions are partitioned by behavior, with one generated depth case retained strictly as stress.
- The static module-specifier evaluator now dispatches its ordered call evaluators through one typed resolver table instead of a 70-handler copy-pasted chain. Representative first, middle, and final resolver families retain native end-to-end coverage.
- E2E high-cardinality sources can now be generated from validated declarative specs, and filtered runs materialize `node_modules` fixtures only when a selected case references them, keeping unrelated filtered tests from rewriting the working tree.

- Verified bounded fs write/append encoding coverage: `fs.writeFileSync`, `fs.appendFileSync`, libuv-backed `fs.promises.writeFile` / `appendFile`, and `fs.promises.open` FileHandle `writeFile()` / `appendFile()` now accept direct and object-literal ASCII, Latin-1, and binary string encodings alongside UTF-8/hex/base64. Test: `fs_write_append_additional_encodings`.
- Verified bounded FileHandle `readFile()` cancellation coverage: libuv-backed `fs.promises.open` handles now accept `{ signal }` options, reject pending and pre-aborted reads through the existing cancellation path, and preserve the caller-owned descriptor for explicit close. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_read_file_abort`.
- Verified bounded FileHandle write/append cancellation coverage: libuv-backed `fs.promises.open` handles now accept `{ signal }` options for `writeFile()` and `appendFile()`, reject pending and pre-aborted writes through the existing cancellation path, and preserve the caller-owned descriptor for explicit close. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_write_append_abort`.
- Verified bounded FileHandle Buffer I/O options coverage: libuv-backed `fs.promises.open` handles now accept `{ offset, length, position }` objects for `read()` and `write()`, including nullable current-position reads and Node-compatible default lengths, through the existing asynchronous I/O path. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_io_options`.
- Verified bounded FileHandle options-only read coverage: libuv-backed `fs.promises.open` handles now accept `read({ buffer?, offset?, length?, position? })`, including a caller-provided Buffer and a zero-filled 16 KiB default Buffer, through the existing asynchronous I/O path. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_read_options`.
- `fs.promises.open` FileHandle `readLines({ autoClose })` now closes the underlying descriptor by default when the iterator exhausts, is returned, or fails, while `autoClose: false` preserves the caller-owned descriptor for later use. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_read_lines_autoclose`.
- `fs.promises.open` FileHandle `readLines({ emitClose })` now exposes EventEmitter-compatible iterator listeners and emits one `close` event on exhaustion, return, or read failure by default, while `emitClose: false` suppresses that event. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_read_lines_emit_close`.

- `fs.promises.open` FileHandle `readLines({ encoding })` now accepts UTF-8, ASCII, Latin-1/binary, hex, and base64 encodings, preserving byte-aware line behavior for decoded encodings and encoded output for hex/base64. Test: `fs_promises_file_handle_read_lines_encoding`.

- Bounded `https` / `node:https` client transport now performs OpenSSL TLS negotiation over the native nonblocking socket runtime, supports `request` / `get` with `hostname` / `host` / `port` / `path` / `method` / `headers` plus `rejectUnauthorized` and `servername`, and reuses the existing bounded HTTP/1.1 response parser and request streaming surface. Concurrent pooling, chunked keep-alive reuse, general backpressure, and `http2` remain deferred. Test: `https_client_transport`.
- Bounded HTTP/HTTPS client AbortSignal support now covers pre-aborted and in-flight `http.request` / `http.get` calls plus the shared `https.request` path, defers cancellation so listeners observe the signal reason as one request error, and keeps the controller/signal graph rooted under normal GC. Broader AbortSignal exception-channel semantics remain deferred. Tests: `http_request_signal`, `https_request_signal`.
- Bounded HTTP/HTTPS client authentication support now accepts an `auth` option on `http.request` / `http.get` and the shared `https.request` / `https.get` path, synthesizes a Basic `Authorization` header when callers do not provide one, and preserves an explicit authorization header. Broader proxy, agent, and credential negotiation semantics remain deferred. Tests: `http_request_auth`, `https_client_transport`.
- `child_process.spawn(file, args?, options?)` now creates a real asynchronous POSIX child with pipe-backed stdin/stdout/stderr, dynamic EventEmitter-compatible `.on` / `.once` / removal methods, `data` / `end` stream events, `spawn` / `exit` / `close` lifecycle events, stream `setEncoding("utf8")`, stdin `write` / `end`, and `kill` / exit-signal state across named, namespace, and default module forms; broader spawn options, `fork`, cluster, worker threads, and Windows behavior remain deferred. Tests: `child_process_spawn`, `child_process_spawn_streams`, `child_process_spawn_kill`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` handles now expose launch metadata through `spawnfile` and a boxed `spawnargs` array containing the requested file and argument list across the child lifecycle. Broader async child metadata and lifecycle semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_metadata`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` now gates the `spawn` event on a successful POSIX exec, emits one launch error without `spawn` when setup/exec reports failure, and preserves `error` before `exit` / `close` for failed children. Broader async lifecycle and error-object semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_error`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` handles now expose a live `stdio` array aliasing `[stdin, stdout, stderr]`, with `null` entries for ignored or inherited descriptors. Broader async child metadata and stdio descriptor forms remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stdio`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` now accepts `argv0` and POSIX-inert `windowsHide` / `windowsVerbatimArguments` options; `argv0` is forwarded to the launched process while the Windows flags preserve portable call-site compatibility. Broader async spawn-option semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_options`.
- Bounded asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` readable-stream piping now forwards stdout/stderr data to one writable destination through `pipe()` / `unpipe()`, returns the destination from `pipe()`, honors `{ end: false }`, ends destinations by default, and resumes a source paused by a false destination write after `drain`. Broader multi-destination and stream lifecycle semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stream_pipe`.
- Bounded asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` `ref()` / `unref()` support now toggles whether child polling and timeout handles keep the runtime event loop alive; unrefed children can outlive the parent’s refed work, and `ref()` restores the default keep-alive behavior. Broader async child lifecycle semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_ref_unref`.
- Bounded asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` AbortSignal support now kills a POSIX child with the configured `killSignal`, emits the signal reason once before `exit` / `close`, suppresses `spawn` for pre-aborted signals, and preserves `killed` state. Broader AbortSignal exception-channel semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_signal`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` stdin streams now use nonblocking 16 KiB backpressure queues, expose synchronized `writableHighWaterMark` / `writableLength` / `writableNeedDrain` / `writableEnded` state, invoke queued `write()` and `end()` callbacks, emit `drain` / `finish`, and report one `error` event when a closed or failed pipe rejects a write. Broader async child lifecycle, spawn-option, and stream read/backpressure semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stream_backpressure`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` stdout/stderr streams now implement bounded `pause()` / `resume()` read gates, preserve unread pipe data while paused, and expose synchronized `readable`, `readableEnded`, `readableFlowing`, `paused`, and `isPaused()` state. Broader async child lifecycle, stream backpressure, and read-error semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stream_pause_resume`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` streams now accept bounded `destroy(error?, callback?)` calls, close their native pipe, deliver one supplied error value, and invoke the destroy callback with the same error while preserving destroyed/readable state. Repeated destruction is callback-safe without re-emitting the error. Broader async child lifecycle and stream read-error semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stream_destroy`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` streams now emit one `close` event after readable EOF or explicit destruction, preserving `data` / `end` / stream-close ordering and error-before-close destruction delivery. Broader async child lifecycle and stream read-error semantics remain deferred. Tests: `child_process_spawn_stream_close`, `child_process_spawn_stream_destroy`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(...)` paused stdout/stderr streams now support bounded nonblocking `read(size?)` pulls, including zero-size reads, UTF-8/Buffer result paths, and EOF/close transitions without emitting duplicate `data` events. Broader async child lifecycle and stream read/backpressure/error semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_stream_read`.
- Asynchronous `child_process.spawn(file, args?, { timeout, killSignal })` now terminates unfinished POSIX children after the numeric timeout, sets the child `killed` state, preserves normal `exit` / `close` signal reporting, and cancels the timeout when the child closes. Broader async lifecycle and spawn-option semantics remain deferred. Test: `child_process_spawn_timeout`.
- Bounded HTTP/1.1 server keep-alive now accepts sequential requests with explicit `Connection: keep-alive` and `Content-Length` bodies on one native TCP connection, preserves unread pipelined bytes, emits `Connection: keep-alive` responses, and closes when a final request uses `Connection: close`; chunked keep-alive reuse and backpressure remain deferred. Test: `http_keep_alive`.
- `http` / `node:http` now support bounded HTTP/1.1 chunked request and response transfer over native TCP, decoding request chunks and response trailers while encoding buffered client/server bodies by default when `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is selected. Explicit request/response streaming is covered separately; broader keep-alive/chunked pooling and general streaming/backpressure remain deferred. Test: `http_chunked_transport`.
- Explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` HTTP server responses now flush each `write()` as a framed chunk, and client response objects expose `data` / `end` events while maintaining the compatibility `body` field; broader keep-alive/chunked pooling and general streaming/backpressure remain deferred. Test: `http_response_streaming`.
- Explicit chunked HTTP `ServerResponse.write()` calls now propagate the underlying 16 KiB socket backpressure result, expose synchronized writable high-water state, and forward `drain` through response EventEmitter listeners. Broader HTTP client/request backpressure, chunked keep-alive reuse, and general streaming remain deferred. Test: `http_response_backpressure`.
- Explicit chunked HTTP `ClientRequest.write()` calls now report queued 16 KiB backpressure before and after connection, expose synchronized writable high-water state, and forward socket `drain` through request EventEmitter listeners. Broader HTTP pooling, chunked keep-alive reuse, and general streaming remain deferred. Test: `http_request_backpressure`.
- Sequential chunked HTTP client requests and framed chunked responses now reuse one endpoint-keyed idle connection, preserve exact server-side chunk consumption, and discard non-reusable pooled sockets after close-delimited responses. Concurrent pooling, pipelining, and broader streaming remain deferred. Test: `http_chunked_keep_alive_pool`.
- Explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` HTTP client requests now preserve individual `write()` calls as wire-level chunks before the terminating chunk, while ordinary requests remain buffered; broader keep-alive/chunked pooling and general streaming/backpressure remain deferred. Test: `http_request_streaming`.
- `http.request(options, callback?)` and `http.get(options, callback?)` now provide bounded HTTP/1.1 client transport over native TCP with endpoint-keyed sequential keep-alive reuse for ordinary non-chunked requests: options cover `hostname` / `host` / `port` / `path` / `method` / `headers` / `auth` / `signal`, requests buffer string/Buffer `write` / `end`, `get` auto-ends, and responses expose status/version/headers/body metadata. Concurrent pooling, chunked keep-alive reuse, streaming, and `http2` remain deferred. Tests: `http_client_transport`, `http_client_keep_alive_pool`.
- `http.createServer(requestListener?)` now provides a bounded HTTP/1.1 server transport over the native TCP runtime: it parses request lines, lower-case headers, and `Content-Length` bodies, invokes the request listener with request metadata and a response object, supports response status, headers, `writeHead`, `write`, `end`, and server close lifecycle behavior, and supports sequential `Connection: keep-alive` requests. Chunked keep-alive reuse, streaming, and `http2` remain deferred. Tests: `http_server_transport`, `http_keep_alive`.
- `http` / `node:http` header validation exports now validate token names and header content across named, namespace, and default forms, including evaluation of optional labels and ignored trailing arguments; broader keep-alive/chunked pooling, streaming behavior, and `http2` remain deferred. Test: `http_header_validation`.
- `http` / `node:http` metadata imports now expose the complete `METHODS` array, the complete `STATUS_CODES` map, and `maxHeaderSize` across named, namespace, and default import forms; broader keep-alive/chunked pooling, streaming behavior, and `http2` remain deferred. Test: `http_metadata`.

Everything in this file compiles end-to-end to a native binary via `./bin/tsc2c file.ts -o out`. Each bullet points at the test case under `tests/e2e/cases/` that exercises it and, where useful, at the runtime symbol or emitter method that implements it.

Full-suite verification, when deliberately needed: `TSC2C_NO_GC=1 bun tests/e2e/run.ts`. Normal change rounds should prefer focused `--filter` slices.

---

- Optional GCD-style dispatch concurrency (requires libdispatch when used; zero impact otherwise): serial `new DispatchQueue(label)` and shared `DispatchQueue.concurrent()` queues, `dispatch.async(queue, () => value)` running the task on a worker thread and resolving a Promise on the main event loop, and blocking `dispatch.sync(queue, () => value)` with same-serial-queue deadlock detection. Task throws propagate as rejections (`async`) or rethrows (`sync`). Compile-time capture discipline: tasks capture only const primitives/DispatchQueue references and may not use `await`, `this`, or be async. Runtime: `runtime/tsc_dispatch.c` + `TSC_THREADS` hooks in `tsc_core.c` (emitter: `emitDispatchCall`). Tests: `dispatch_async_basic`, `dispatch_error_propagation`, `dispatch_capture_const_diagnostic`, `dispatch_await_diagnostic`
- Branch-block source-try structural conditional returns now reuse the generic sequence adapter for bounded multi-await structural arms selected by simple nested conditional selectors, preserving structural values, source rejection, catch recovery, and synchronous `finally` cleanup across async declarations, class methods, and async-arrow function values. Test: `async_await_branch_block_source_try_conditional_mixed_sync_await`.

- Ordinary awaited iterator bodies now sequence multiple direct awaited source-`try` statements, route body rejection into awaited catch recovery, run a synchronous `finally` once after fulfilled body/catch paths, and preserve catch rejection after synchronous cleanup for both `for…of` and `for…in`; broader source try control-flow graphs remain deferred. - Ordinary awaited iterator bodies now sequence multiple direct awaited source-`try` statements, run a synchronous `finally` once after full fulfillment and after rejection from any try await before propagating that rejection for both `for…of` and `for…in`; broader source try control-flow graphs remain deferred. - Source `try`/`finally` pending-`await` finally-prelude locals are preserved for lifted async function values and nested async closures. Test: `async_await_try_catch_values`

## 1. Language core

### Literals
- Numeric literals — decimal, `0x`/`0o`/`0b`, underscore separators → `formatNumericLiteral` in `src/emit/index.ts`. Test: `arith`
- BigInt literals (`0n`, `0xfn`, `0o77n`, `0b101n`), `BigInt(value, ...ignored)`, arithmetic/comparison/equality, unary minus, compound arithmetic assignment, `typeof`, `.toString(radix?, ...ignored)` with explicit `undefined` defaulting to radix 10 after evaluating ignored extras, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, `.valueOf(...ignored)`, and inherited `hasOwnProperty(prop, ...ignored)` / `propertyIsEnumerable(prop, ...ignored)` backed by GMP, with catchable constructor/operator/radix validation failures. Tests: `bigint`, `bigint_errors`, `symbol_bigint_object_methods`
- Symbol values via `Symbol(description?, ...ignored)`, where explicit `undefined` creates a symbol with no description while ignored extras still evaluate, `Symbol.for(key, ...ignored)`, `Symbol.keyFor(sym, ...ignored)`, `Symbol.iterator`, `Symbol.asyncIterator`, `Symbol.dispose`, `Symbol.asyncDispose`, `Symbol.toStringTag`, `Symbol.species`, `.description`, `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, `.valueOf(...ignored)`, inherited `hasOwnProperty(prop, ...ignored)` / `propertyIsEnumerable(prop, ...ignored)`, equality, and `typeof`. Tests: `symbols`, `symbol_bigint_object_methods`
- String literals with full C escape handling for UTF-8 and non-BMP code points → `escapeCString` in `src/emit/cbuf.ts`. Test: `hello`, `strings`, `string_for_of`
- Runtime string allocations initialize cached hash metadata before dynamic object, map, and JSON-derived string-key lookups use hash-based buckets, and string equality skips byte comparison when both cached hashes are known to differ. Test: `string_hash_dynamic_keys`
- Template literals with `${expr}` interpolation evaluate substitutions left-to-right → `emitTemplate`. Tests: `greet`, `fizzbuzz`, `template_literal_eval_order`
- Tagged template calls with a `TemplateStringsArray` first parameter and fixed substitution parameters. Test: `tagged_templates`
- `String.raw` tagged templates preserve raw template segments and stringify compile-time or dynamic substitutions left-to-right. Tests: `string_raw`, `string_raw_dynamic`
- Boolean literals `true` / `false`. Test: `json`
- `null` / `undefined` / `NaN` / `Infinity` globals, with inferred top-level and local nullish variables stored as boxed values so `typeof` and strict equality preserve JavaScript null-vs-undefined identity, and uninitialized dynamic variables defaulting to JavaScript `undefined` in top-level, local, and captured storage. Tests: `nullish`, `stdlib_os`, `nullish_variable_storage`, `uninitialized_dynamic_variables`
- Array literals `[1, 2, 3]` with spread `[0, ...a, 6]` → `emitArrayLiteral`. Test: `advanced`
- Object literals `{ x: 1 }` matched against an interface/class shape → `emitObjectLiteral`. Test: `interfaces`
- Computed property names in typed object literals when the key resolves to a string/number literal, e.g. `{ [key]: value }`. Test: `computed_props`
- Regex literals `/pattern/flags` → `emitExpr` RegularExpressionLiteral branch. Tests: `regex`, `regex_pcre2`

- Callable `String(value?, ...ignored)` returns JS-style string coercion for typed and dynamic values while evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_boolean_constructors`

### Operators
- Arithmetic: `+ - * / % **` (incl. `tsc_num_mod` for JS-semantics modulo, `pow` for `**`)
- Comparison: `== != === !==` (with `tsc_str_eq` for strings)
- Relational: `< <= > >=` (with `tsc_str_cmp` for strings)
- Logical: `&& || !`
- Bitwise: `& | ^ << >> >>>` (JS-style int32 semantics)
- Assignment + compound: `= += -= *= /= %= **= &= |= ^= <<= >>= >>>= &&= ||= ??=`; typed `string` LHS supports `+=` with any rhs through `tsc_str_concat` plus implicit string coercion, and dynamic property/index lvalues support descriptor-aware exponent/bitwise/logical assignment. Tests: `string_compound_plus`, `bitwise_assign`, `exponent_assign`, `logical_assign`, `dynamic_bitwise_ops`, `dynamic_property_logical_assign`
- Pre/post `++` `--`; local dynamic `any` variables plus dynamic property and index lvalues use JS-style numeric coercion and preserve prefix/postfix expression results. Test: `dynamic_update_ops`
- `typeof` in typed code — JS type string with operand side effects preserved. Nullable pointer unions such as `string | null` and `string | undefined` produce the nullish runtime result and work in equality/inequality guards; dynamic primitive unions such as `string | number | boolean` narrow through the existing unbox bridge. Tests: `typeof`, `typeof_guards`, `typeof_boolean_union`
- `void expr` evaluates `expr` for side effects and yields `undefined`, including expression-bodied function values that return `any` from a side-effectful `void` expression before boxing the result as `undefined`. Tests: `void_operator`, `object_prototype_accessor_nullish_call`
- Side-effect-free `void` expressions participate in the static undefined/nullish/falsy analysis used by generated-C DCE. Test: `static_void_analysis`
- Comma operator expressions evaluate left-to-right and return the right-hand value. Test: `comma_operator`
- TypeScript-only `expr satisfies T`, `expr as T`, `<T>expr`, and `expr!` assertions erase to the runtime operand. Test: `satisfies_expression`
- The local no-lib TypeScript shim declares the standard `Record<K, T>` utility type, which erases to ordinary object runtime behavior. Test: `utility_record_type`
- Ternary `a ? b : c`
- Nullish coalescing `??` — null-aware for pointer types. Test: `nullish`
- Optional chaining `?.` — null-aware for class fields with zero-sentinel fallback. Test: `nullish`
- Cross-type null comparison: `arr !== null`, `cls === null`
- `instanceof` for class instances across single-inheritance chains. Test: `instanceof`
- `key in obj` works for dynamic objects and typed interface/class field lists, and participates in union narrowing for interface-shaped dynamic unions. Tests: `dynamic_property_ops`, `object_prototypes`, `in_operator_narrowing`

## 2. Functions

- Promise settlement now retains a decoded GC-visible pointer beside every NaN-boxed string, array, object, or function result (including rejection reasons), so queued async callbacks cannot observe reclaimed payloads after allocation pressure. Covered by `promise_gc_result_root` and the default-GC `async_await_while_condition` corpus.
- Async continuation parameters of dynamic type carry decoded companion roots in heap state, and async declarations, methods, and lifted arrows root dynamic parameters on entry plus initialized and assigned-before-use dynamic prelude locals through continuation transfer. Mutable closure captures use paired shared value/root cells, so closure aliases retain and update the same decoded root on reassignment. Dynamic object data/accessor slots retain nested NaN-boxed payloads, and pointer-bearing `Set` storage is conservatively scanned. Exception landing paths own the single matching try-frame pop instead of double-popping after `longjmp`. Semantic GC/lifetime partitions and the representative generated depth stress cover the affected alias, container, and completion paths.
- Awaited loop bodies now carry typed completion edges in the shared async IR: `continue` targets loop-condition re-entry, `break` targets loop fallthrough, and `return` / `throw` target function settlement. The former primary/alternate continue, break, and rejection flag pairs have been removed; `async_await_while_condition`, `multi_condition`, `conditional_condition`, and `async_await_loop_condition_graph` cover the migrated routes.
- Leading-await statement chains now use `AsyncStatementSuspensionGraph`: each await has an arbitrary-cardinality state ID, explicit state/completion successor, and owned interstitial statement block, while one typed function-completion edge represents awaited or synchronous `return` / `throw`. This replaces the parallel step/interstitial arrays and four independent terminal fields; covered by the `leading` family, `async_await_eight_step_chain`, try/catch/finally chains, and loop-leading capture coverage.
- Async try/catch/finally continuations represent successful and caught terminals as `AsyncFunctionCompletionEdge` values. Conditional and sequence specialization retain the original source completion statement while retargeting the staged value; direct, finally-only, combined try/catch/finally, leading, and shared staged adapters dispatch on typed `return` / `throw` kinds instead of parallel expression fields. The remaining Boolean records only whether settlement consumes the staged awaited value. The 12-case `async_await_try_catch` family, four-case `async_await_try_finally` family, awaited-return branches, five-await throws, and broad pending-return corpus cover the migrated routes.
- Async closure continuations retain captured bindings as `tsc_async_cell_ref_t` handles containing the shared value-cell and decoded-root-cell pointers, rather than snapshotting their values. Handles copy through arbitrary continuation state transfers, reads dereference the current cell, and closures created after a suspension capture the current handle; binding reassignment therefore remains observable across one or multiple pending awaits while preserving dynamic GC roots. Nested closure implementations prioritize their own environment over outer adapter scopes. Covered by the single- and multi-suspension rebinding paths in `async_closure_direct_await_capture`, plus `async_await_eight_step_chain`, `function_closures`, and `async_dynamic_container_gc_root`.
- Caught awaits whose inferred fulfillment type is `never` but whose value is unused lower through the try/catch continuation with void storage instead of generic immediate-await emission. Combined try/catch/finally continuations now carry explicit fulfilled-try and caught-rejection fallthrough flags plus one shared post-finally completion; both branches execute their post-await statements, converge through cleanup, and evaluate the outer `return` only after `finally`. With the sibling paths unified, already-settled sources queue every migrated adapter instead of resuming synchronously. Covered by `async_await_settled_microtask_order`, the 12-case `async_await_try_catch` ordering/fallthrough matrix, and pending-return stress.

- Top-level `function` declarations with typed params and return. Test: `greet`
- Default-initialized parameters are supported for omitted trailing arguments on top-level functions, constructors, instance methods, and static methods when the default expression may reference earlier parameters and does not reference `this`, `arguments`, or the same or a later parameter, including function-typed defaults initialized from arrow/function closure values. Omitted optional parameters without defaults are supported for pointer-like and dynamic parameter types, including strings, arrays, classes, function-typed parameters, and first-class closure values; numeric/boolean optional parameters still require explicit defaults. Tests: `default_parameters`, `default_parameter_function_initializers`, `optional_parameters`, `closure_optional_parameters`
- Explicit `this: void` function parameters are treated as compile-time-only markers and omitted from the generated function ABI for direct calls, function-typed values, and higher-order callbacks. Test: `function_this_void`
- Recursion (direct)
- Top-level `const f = (...) => ...` **lifted to a static C function** — usable both as a call target and as an HOF callback. Test: `fn_refs`
- Inline arrow functions in HOF call sites, including expression bodies and single-return block bodies (body expanded inline via GCC statement expressions). Test: `array_hof`
- Function references passed as HOF callbacks — both declared functions and lifted-arrow consts. Test: `fn_refs`
- First-class typed closures for arrow/function expressions that capture enclosing function-scope locals or parameters. Captured storage is boxed in GC-managed ref cells and closure values lower to generated `{fn, env}` structs per signature; calls through function-typed values support spread arguments from dynamic arrays/strings with runtime arity checks and omitted optional pointer-like/dynamic parameters without defaults. Tests: `function_closures`, `function_value_spread`, `closure_optional_parameters`
- Direct calls to top-level generic functions are monomorphized per concrete call signature, with simple `T` and `T[]` annotations inside the function body and fixed-arity spread argument lists. Test: `generic_functions`
- Top-level generic function references are specialized in typed array callback contexts such as `map(identity)`, `flatMap(wrap)`, `filter`, `reduce`, `forEach`, `find`/`some`/`every`, and `sort` comparators. Test: `generic_callbacks`
- Top-level generic function references are specialized when assigned to concrete function-typed values, using generated adapter closures. Test: `generic_function_values`
- `Reflect.apply(fn, thisArg, args)` works for statically known function values with array-literal, array-literal-spread, typed-array, and dynamic-array argument lists; function values that declare `this: any` receive the supplied `thisArg`. Test: `reflect_apply`
- Dynamic function values support `.call(...)` and `.apply(...)` lowering through the boxed function dispatcher for generic function identities and callable proxies, including array-like `.apply(...)` argument-list objects plus omitted, `undefined`, and `null` `.apply(...)` argument lists; `Function.apply(...)` also evaluates and ignores trailing arguments after the optional argument list. Tests: `function_call_apply_defaults`, `proxy_revocable_revoke_function`
- Dynamic `Function.apply(...)` method calls reject non-array-like argument-list values through catchable runtime exceptions while preserving valid array-like argument objects. Test: `function_call_apply_validation`
- Dynamic function values preserve ordinary own string-key and numeric-key properties, including huge numeric keys formatted with JavaScript-style number-to-string conversion, alongside `length`, `name`, and `prototype`; assignment, deletion, Object/Reflect own-key helpers, descriptors, extensibility/seal/freeze, and `Object.assign` targets observe those properties. Test: `dynamic_function_own_properties`
- Boxed function `name` and `length` are standard configurable, non-writable, non-enumerable own properties with deletion, redefinition, sealing/freezing, own-key ordering, and Proxy invariant behavior delegated through the ordinary property store; constructable `prototype` remains writable and non-configurable metadata. Test: `function_integrity`

## 3. Classes & types

- `class Foo { field: T; }` — compiled to a C struct; string/number literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed field names are accepted. Tests: `classes`, `class_computed_members`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`
- Constructors — `ClassName_init(self, ...)` + `ClassName_new(...)` pair; fixed-arity constructor calls accept spread argument lists. Test: `classes`
- Methods — `ClassName_methodName(self, ...)`; string/number literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed method names are accepted. Tests: `classes`, `class_computed_members`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`
- `this` → `self` inside methods and ctor
- `new Foo(args)` / `new Foo(...args)` → `Foo_new(args)`. Test: `classes`
- `Reflect.construct(Foo, args)` works for statically known class constructors with array-literal, array-literal-spread, typed-array, and dynamic-array argument lists, including standard class decorator replacement constructors for ordinary and erased generic classes. Tests: `reflect_construct`, `class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `generic_class_decorator_reflect_construct`
- `Reflect.preventExtensions(...)` boxes primitive and typed class targets through the existing dynamic target path, rejects fixed built-in targets with a precise compile-time diagnostic, and preserves runtime object-target validation for primitives. Tests: `reflect_object_target_validation`, `reflect_fixed_builtin_prevent_reject`
- Field access `obj.x`, field assignment `obj.x = v`. Test: `classes`
- Named class getter and setter accessors lower to C calls for instance and static property reads/writes, including string/number literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed accessor names. Plain setter assignments, numeric/string compound setter assignments, and logical setter assignments return the JavaScript assignment value. Tests: `class_accessors_basic`, `class_accessors_compound`, `class_accessors_logical`, `class_computed_accessors`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`
- **Single inheritance** via `extends` — base fields laid out at struct head for safe up-cast. Test: `inheritance`
- `super(...)` call in subclass constructor → `Base_init((Base_t*)self, ...)`. Test: `inheritance`
- **Static fields** — emitted as file-scope `ClassName_field` storage and initialized in module init, including computed names. Tests: `inheritance`, `class_computed_members`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`
- **Static initialization blocks** — emitted in member order with static field initializers during module initialization. Test: `class_static_blocks`
- **Static methods** — called as `ClassName_method(args)`, including computed names. Tests: `inheritance`, `class_computed_members`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`
- Standard class decorators on named classes are evaluated during module initialization. Direct decorator functions, decorator-factory closure results, and dynamic callable/proxy-backed decorators receive a dynamic context object with `kind: "class"`, `name`, `metadata`, and `addInitializer`; multiple decorator expressions on the same class evaluate top-down and invoke bottom-up. Class decorators can return AOT constructor replacement functions used by direct `new Class(...)` calls, parenthesized constructor targets, inferred constructor aliases used through direct `new`, parenthesized `new`, or static `Reflect.construct(...)`, chained aliases for erased generic class constructors, decorated class binding reads used as dynamic constructor values, and static `Reflect.construct(Class, args)` targets, including spread constructor calls and erased generic class constructors, stacked class decorator replacements compose in bottom-up invocation order while forwarding constructor arguments, and the original class value passed to decorators is constructible through `Reflect.construct(value, args)`. Broader class replacement edge cases remain deferred. Tests: `class_decorator_basic`, `class_decorator_factory`, `class_decorator_replacement`, `class_decorator_alias_replacement`, `class_decorator_dynamic_value_replacement`, `class_decorator_parenthesized_replacement`, `class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `class_decorator_replacement_order`, `generic_class_decorator_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_alias_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `decorator_add_initializer_basic`, `decorator_proxy_basic`, `decorator_replacement_order`, `decorator_factory_order`
- Standard method decorators on named instance and static methods are evaluated during module initialization. Direct decorator functions and dynamic callable/proxy-backed decorators receive a dynamic context object with `kind`, `name`, `static`, `private`, `metadata`, and `addInitializer`; multiple decorator expressions on the same method evaluate top-down and invoke bottom-up; static method decorators can return replacement functions used by direct `Class.method(...)` calls, and instance method decorators can return replacement functions used by direct `obj.method(...)` calls with the actual instance passed to typed class `this` receivers. Static and instance method replacements can call the original method value through `Reflect.apply(value, thisArg, args)`, and proxy-backed method decorators can return replacement functions through the dynamic decorator apply path. Literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed method names are covered. Tests: `method_decorator_basic`, `static_method_decorator_replacement`, `static_decorator_originals`, `instance_method_decorator_replacement`, `instance_method_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_method_decorator_original`, `decorator_computed_members`, `decorator_computed_nonliteral_members`, `decorator_add_initializer_basic`, `decorator_proxy_basic`, `decorator_proxy_replacement`, `decorator_replacement_order`, `decorator_factory_order`
- Standard field decorators on named instance and static fields are evaluated during module initialization. Direct decorator functions receive a dynamic context object with `kind`, `name`, `static`, `private`, `metadata`, and `addInitializer`; returned initializer functions transform instance and static field initial values, and multiple returned initializers apply top-down after bottom-up decorator invocation. Literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed field names are covered. Tests: `field_decorator_basic`, `field_decorator_initializer`, `field_decorator_initializer_order`, `decorator_computed_members`, `decorator_computed_nonliteral_members`, `decorator_proxy_basic`
- Standard getter and setter decorators on named instance and static accessors are evaluated during module initialization. Direct decorator functions receive a dynamic context object with `kind`, `name`, `static`, `private`, `metadata`, and `addInitializer`; static getter decorators can return replacement getter functions used by direct `Class.property` reads, static setter decorators can return replacement setter functions used by direct `Class.property = value` writes, instance getter and setter decorators can return replacement functions used by direct `obj.property` reads/writes with the actual instance passed to typed class `this` receivers. Static and instance getter/setter replacements can call the original accessor value through `Reflect.apply(value, thisArg, args)`. Literal, const-literal, and asserted static-expression computed accessor names are covered. Tests: `accessor_decorator_basic`, `static_getter_decorator_replacement`, `static_setter_decorator_replacement`, `static_decorator_originals`, `instance_getter_decorator_replacement`, `instance_getter_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_getter_decorator_original`, `instance_setter_decorator_replacement`, `instance_setter_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_setter_decorator_original`, `decorator_computed_members`, `decorator_computed_nonliteral_members`, `decorator_proxy_basic`
- Standard decorator contexts expose a shared dynamic `metadata` object for all decorators on a named class during module initialization. Test: `decorator_metadata_basic`
- Inherited method dispatch — `d.describe()` on `Dog extends Animal` resolves to `Animal_describe((Animal_t*)d)`. Test: `inheritance`
- `abstract` classes, access modifiers, and `readonly` fields are accepted as TS-only modifiers. Test: `class_modifiers`
- `interface` declarations → C struct types (no runtime overhead); `extends` emits inherited fields in base-first order for field access and typed Object/Reflect field-list helpers. Tests: `interfaces`, `interface_inheritance`
- Object literals typed against an interface/class → allocated + field-assigned. Test: `interfaces`
- Non-escaping local typed object literals that only flow through same-block property reads/writes are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc`
- Non-escaping local typed object literals and `new Class(...)` values used as targets for read-only Object/Reflect/Object-prototype inspection helpers, including extensibility and integrity inspectors, are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc_helpers`
- Non-escaping local typed object literals and `new Class(...)` values that flow through same-block alias chains remain stack-allocated when the aliases only use safe property access and read-only inspections. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc_alias`
- Non-escaping local typed object literals and `new Class(...)` values that flow through same-block assignment alias chains remain stack-allocated when the aliases only use safe property access and read-only inspections. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc_alias_assignment_direct`
- Non-escaping local typed object literals and `new Class(...)` values that flow through `Object.prototype.valueOf.call(...)` remain stack-allocated when the returned receiver stays within safe same-block property access and inspection uses. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc_value_of`
- Closure-captured local typed object literals and same-block aliases fall back to heap storage so returned/nested closures cannot retain stack-backed object storage. Test: `object_literal_stack_alloc_closure_capture`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals that only flow through same-block element reads/writes and readonly `.length` reads are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through receiver-safe readonly/copying array methods such as `join(...)` are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_method`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through non-growing mutating methods `pop(...)` and `shift(...)` are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_mutation`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through ignored receiver-returning in-place methods such as `reverse(...)`, `fill(...)`, and `copyWithin(...)` are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_in_place`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through same-block, non-loop `push(...)` / `unshift(...)` calls are stack-allocated with finite extra capacity for inserted elements instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_growth`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through same-block `for...of` and `for...in` iteration are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_iteration`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals whose receiver-returning in-place methods are consumed immediately by safe reads or readonly/copying methods are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_chained`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used through independent iterator-array helpers `keys(...)`, `values(...)`, and `entries(...)` are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_iterators`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals used as targets for supported read-only Object/Reflect helper calls and `in` checks are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_object_helpers`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals passed through read-only `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...)`, `isPrototypeOf.call(...)`, `propertyIsEnumerable.call(...)`, `toLocaleString.call(...)`, and `toString.call(...)` inspection forms are stack-allocated instead of GC-allocated. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_object_prototype_call`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals whose receiver-returning in-place method results are captured by same-block aliases remain stack-allocated when those aliases only flow through safe reads and inspections. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_alias`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals whose receiver-returning in-place method results are assigned to local variables (including inside nested blocks) remain stack-allocated when those assignment aliases only flow through safe reads and inspections. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_alias_assignment`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals that flow through same-block direct alias chains remain stack-allocated when those aliases only use safe reads, inspections, non-growing mutations, and finite `push(...)` / `unshift(...)` growth. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_alias_direct`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals that flow through same-block assignment alias chains remain stack-allocated when those aliases only use safe reads, inspections, non-growing mutations, and finite `push(...)` / `unshift(...)` growth. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_alias_assignment_direct`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals grown by `push(...)` / `unshift(...)` inside simple finite counted `for` loops are stack-allocated with statically reserved capacity. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_loop_growth`
- Non-escaping local typed array literals that flow through `Object.prototype.valueOf.call(...)` remain stack-allocated when the returned receiver is consumed only by read-only safe uses or same-block aliases. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_value_of`
- Local typed array literals referenced from nested callbacks fall back to heap storage so callback-driven `push(...)` growth cannot reallocate stack-backed buffers. Test: `array_literal_stack_alloc_callback_growth`
- Interface nesting — `interface Line { from: Point; to: Point; }`. Test: `interfaces`
- Shorthand property assignment `{ x, y }`. Test: `interfaces`
- Computed property assignment with literal or const-literal keys. Test: `computed_props`
- Numeric `enum` declarations and `Enum.Member` constants. Test: `enums`

## 4. Collections

### Arrays
- Literal construction with optional `...spread`. Test: `advanced`
- Index access `arr[i]` (get and set) via `TSC_ARR(T, arr, i)` macro
- `.length` → `tsc_array_length`
- `.push(...)` / `.pop(...ignored)` — `tsc_array_push_raw`, `tsc_array_pop_raw`; ignored `pop` arguments are evaluated before being discarded. Test: `arrays`
- `.shift(...ignored)` / `.unshift(...)` — `tsc_array_shift_raw`, `tsc_array_unshift_raw`; ignored `shift` arguments are evaluated before being discarded. Test: `arrays`
- `.reverse(...ignored)` — in-place via `tsc_array_reverse` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `arrays`
- `.toReversed(...ignored)` — copy via `tsc_array_to_reversed`; original array remains unchanged and ignored extra arguments are evaluated. Test: `array_to_reversed`
- `.fill(value, start?, end?, ...ignored)` — in-place via `tsc_array_fill`, including explicit `undefined` defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `array_fill`, `array_mutator_ignored_arguments`
- `.copyWithin(target, start, end?, ...ignored)` — in-place via `tsc_array_copy_within`, including explicit `undefined` end defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `array_copy_within`, `array_mutator_ignored_arguments`
- `.at(index?, ...ignored)` — positive and negative index lookup, defaulting omitted or explicit `undefined` indexes to zero after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `array_at`, `array_read_ignored_arguments`
- `.with(index, value, ...ignored)` — copy via `tsc_array_with` after evaluating ignored extra arguments; original array remains unchanged, negative indices count from the end, and out-of-range failures are catchable. Tests: `array_with`, `array_with_errors`, `array_mutator_ignored_arguments`
- `.splice(start?, deleteCount?, ...items)` — in-place via `tsc_array_splice`, returning removed elements and preserving argument-count semantics for omitted versus explicit `undefined` delete counts. Test: `array_splice`
- `.toSpliced(start?, deleteCount?, ...items)` — copy via `tsc_array_to_spliced`; original array remains unchanged, and explicit `undefined` start/delete-count values use JavaScript defaults while preserving argument-count semantics. Test: `array_to_spliced`
- `.slice(start?, end?, ...ignored)` — `tsc_array_slice`, including explicit `undefined` defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `array_read_ignored_arguments`
- `.concat(...items)` — copy plus `tsc_array_append`/`tsc_array_push_raw`; accepts array arguments, single element arguments, and spread elements inside array-literal arguments, with element-type-agnostic hole preservation through sparse `slice` and append operations. Test: `array_concat_values`
- `.join(sep?, ...ignored)` — with type-driven element stringification, including explicit `undefined` default separators after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `array_read_ignored_arguments`
- `.toString(...ignored)` / `.toLocaleString(...ignored)` — typed arrays reuse comma-join stringification after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `array_to_string`
- `.valueOf(...ignored)` — returns the typed array receiver unchanged after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `array_value_of`
- `.keys(...ignored)` / `.values(...ignored)` / `.entries(...ignored)` — returns a number-index array, a shallow value copy, or `[string, value]` entry arrays after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `array_keys_values`, `array_entries`
- `.hasOwnProperty(key, ...ignored)` / `.propertyIsEnumerable(key, ...ignored)` plus `Object.hasOwn(array, key)`, `Reflect.has(array, key)`, and the `in` operator check typed array indexes and the non-enumerable `length` own property. Direct inherited calls evaluate ignored extra arguments. Tests: `array_own_properties`, `array_object_method_ignored_arguments`
- `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(array, key)`, `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(array)`, and `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(array, key)` return typed array index and `length` data descriptors. Test: `array_property_descriptors`
- `Array.from(string)` — returns an array of one-code-point strings via `tsc_str_chars`. Test: `array_from_string`
- `Array(...items)` / `new Array(...items)` — first-class callable and constructable Array values with stable `Array.prototype.constructor` metadata; a single valid numeric argument creates a bounded dense array of `undefined` values. Test: `array_prototype_constructor`
- Runtime `Array.isArray`, `Array.from`, and `Array.of` static method properties expose standard writable, non-enumerable, configurable descriptors, and detached static calls work through boxed function dispatch. Test: `array_prototype_constructor`
- `.indexOf(x, fromIndex?, ...ignored)`, `.lastIndexOf(x, fromIndex?, ...ignored)`, `.includes(x, fromIndex?, ...ignored)` — with proper per-element-type equality, SameValueZero `includes(NaN)` behavior, JS-style from-index clamping including explicit `undefined` positions, and ignored extra-argument evaluation. Tests: `array_last_index_of`, `array_search_from_index`, `array_includes_same_value_zero`, `array_read_ignored_arguments`
- `.sort(cmp?, ...ignored)` / `.toSorted(cmp?, ...ignored)` — JS-style default string-conversion sort for omitted or explicit `undefined` comparators after evaluating ignored extra arguments; `toSorted` returns a sorted copy. Tests: `array_sort_default`, `array_to_sorted`, `array_sort_ignored_arguments`
- `.sort((a, b) => cmp, ...ignored)` / `.toSorted((a, b) => cmp, ...ignored)` — inline insertion sort after evaluating ignored extra arguments; accepts inline expression-body and single-return block-body callbacks, named function references, and first-class closure comparator values. Tests: `wordcount`, `array_to_sorted`, `array_sort_ignored_arguments`
- `.flat(depth?, ...ignored)` for compile-time numeric depths and explicit `undefined` default depth after evaluating ignored extra arguments, including hole removal from concrete typed outer and inner arrays, plus `.flatMap(cb)` for array-returning or scalar callbacks. Tests: `array_flat`, `array_read_ignored_arguments`
- `.forEach(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.map(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.filter(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.reduce(cb, init, ...ignored)` / `.reduceRight(cb, init, ...ignored)`; non-reduce HOFs evaluate ignored extra arguments after callback and optional `thisArg`, explicit-initial-value reduce forms evaluate ignored extra arguments after the initial value, callbacks receive the standard receiver array argument, inline callbacks may use expression bodies or single-return block bodies, and explicitly `any`-typed `ObjectEntry` callback parameters are boxed for dynamic tuple indexing. Tests: `array_hof`, `array_hof_ignored_arguments`, `array_reduce_ignored_arguments`, `array_reduce_no_initial`, `array_reduce_right`, `object_entries`
- Empty `reduce(...)` / `reduceRight(...)` calls without an initial value throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting, covering typed arrays, dynamic arrays, and detached `Array.prototype` calls on generic array-like receivers. Test: `array_reduce_empty_errors`
- `.find(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.findIndex(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.findLast(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.findLastIndex(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.some(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)` / `.every(cb, thisArg?, ...ignored)`; callbacks receive the standard receiver array argument and inline callbacks may use expression bodies or single-return block bodies. `find` / `findLast` return `undefined` when no element matches for element types that can flow through `tsc_value_t`, including inferred numeric/boolean nullish locals assigned from the result; sparse `find*` callbacks and boxed results use indexed `Get` so deleted slots surface as `undefined`; and predicate/search HOFs evaluate ignored trailing arguments after the optional `thisArg`. Tests: `array_hof`, `array_find_last`, `array_hof_ignored_arguments`, `array_hof_predicate_ignored_arguments`
- Typed array higher-order methods accept optional `thisArg` values, evaluate them once, and bind them for direct and inline callbacks that declare `this: any`. Test: `array_hof_this_arg`
- All HOFs accept **either** inline arrow **or** named function reference, including direct function and closure callback values where supported. Tests: `fn_refs`, `array_hof`
- `for-of` iteration. Test: `arrays`
- `Array.isArray(value, ...ignored)` — resolved at compile time from typed CTypes and at runtime for dynamic values while evaluating ignored trailing arguments, including direct and nested array Proxy chains with revoked-proxy rejection; the stdlib declaration is a type predicate so guarded `unknown` dynamic values narrow to typed array operations. Tests: `advanced`, `array_static_dynamic`, `array_is_array_ignored_arguments`, `array_is_array_narrowing`, `proxy_array_is_array`
- `Array.from(arr)` — identity copy for typed arrays and dynamic `tsc_value_t` arrays. Dynamic strings produce real dynamic arrays of characters, dynamic `null` / `undefined` sources reject through catchable runtime errors after ignored argument evaluation, and non-nullish non-iterable dynamic values return empty arrays in the bounded array-like subset. Tests: `advanced`, `array_static_dynamic`, `array_from_dynamic_edges`
- `Array.from(set)` — typed Set value copy preserving insertion order. Test: `array_from_set`
- `Array.from(map)` — typed `Map<K, V>` entry materialization as `ObjectEntry<V, K>[]` in insertion order, including non-string key entries and dynamic `Map<any, any>` entries. Tests: `array_from_map`, `map_object_entry_constructors`, `map_constructor_dynamic`
- `Array.from(items, mapfn)` / `Array.from(items, mapfn, thisArg)` transforms typed arrays, typed Set sources, typed `Map<K, V>` entry sources, string code-point sequences, and boxed dynamic array/string sources into typed `U[]`, accepting inline arrow/function-expression callbacks with expression bodies or single-return block bodies, plus function references (including generic functions where the source is typed). Dynamic `null` / `undefined` sources reject before mapping, and non-nullish non-iterable dynamic sources map zero elements. Explicit `undefined` mapper arguments take the no-mapper path while preserving optional `thisArg` argument evaluation. Optional mapper `thisArg` values are evaluated once and bound for callbacks that declare `this: any`; boxed mapper parameters over sparse typed arrays use indexed `Get` so deleted slots surface as `undefined`; trailing arguments after the optional `thisArg` are evaluated and ignored. Tests: `array_from_mapper`, `array_from_set`, `array_from_map`, `array_from_dynamic_mapper`, `array_from_dynamic_edges`, `array_from_mapper_this_arg`
- `Array.of(...items)` — typed array construction, including `Array.of<any>(...)` followed by dynamic array coercion. Tests: `array_of`, `dynamic_array_of`

### `Map<K, V>`
- `new Map<K, V>()`, `new Map(Object.entries(obj), ...ignored)`, typed `ObjectEntry<V, K>[]` sources including non-string keys, `new Map(existingMap, ...ignored)` for typed Map sources, and `new Map<any, any>(dynamicSource, ...ignored)` for nullish empty and boxed dynamic array pair sources — `tsc_map_new(sizeof(K), sizeof(V), keyKind, initialCap)`, with supported source constructor extras evaluated and ignored and non-iterable or malformed dynamic sources rejected through catchable runtime errors. Tests: `map_set_constructors`, `map_constructor_from_map`, `map_constructor_dynamic`, `map_object_entry_constructors`, `collection_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- `.set(k, v)`, `.get(k)`, `.has(k)`, `.delete(k)`, `.clear()`; numeric keys use SameValueZero semantics so `NaN` matches `NaN` and `-0` matches `0`, and dynamic-value maps return dynamic `undefined` for missing `.get(...)` keys. Tests: `map_set`, `map_set_same_value_zero`, `map_constructor_dynamic`
- `.keys(...ignored)`, `.values(...ignored)` — returns typed array; `.entries(...ignored)` returns a typed `ObjectEntry<V, K>[]`. Ignored extra arguments are evaluated before being discarded. Tests: `map_entries`, `map_object_entry_constructors`
- `.forEach((value, key, map) => expr, thisArg?, ...ignored)` — inline expression-body or single-return block-body callbacks and named callback references over insertion order; optional `thisArg` values are evaluated once and bound for callbacks that declare `this: any`, and trailing ignored arguments are evaluated before iteration. Tests: `map_set_for_each`, `map_set_for_each_refs`, `map_set_for_each_this_arg`
- Direct `for...of` with `[key, value]` destructuring. Test: `map_set_for_of`
- `.size` property. Test: `map_set`, `wordcount`
- `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)`. Test: `collection_object_methods`
- Key equality is polymorphic by tag: SameValueZero numbers, dynamic values, string content, booleans, and pointers. Runtime: `key_eq`
- ES2024 static `Map.groupBy(...)` groups typed array, typed Set, typed Map entry, string, boxed dynamic array, or boxed dynamic string sources by the callback's return value, returning typed `Map<K, T[]>` groups or `Map<K, ObjectEntry<MV, MK>[]>` for Map sources. Set and Map sources preserve insertion order and string/dynamic-string sources use code-point order for callback index assignment. The callback may be an inline arrow/function expression with an expression body or single-return block body, or a function reference (including generic functions); callbacks that declare `this: any` receive the JavaScript default `undefined` receiver. Trailing arguments after the callback are evaluated and ignored. Tests: `map_group_by`, `map_group_by_dynamic_source`, `group_by_this_param`

### `Set<T>`
- `new Set<T>()`, `new Set(valuesArray, ...ignored)`, `new Set(existingSet, ...ignored)`, and `new Set<any>(dynamicSource, ...ignored)` for nullish empty, boxed dynamic array, and boxed dynamic string sources — `tsc_set_new(sizeof(T), keyKind, initialCap)` plus per-value insertion, with supported source constructor extras evaluated and ignored and non-iterable dynamic sources rejected through catchable runtime errors. Tests: `map_set_constructors`, `set_constructor_from_set`, `set_constructor_dynamic`, `collection_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- `.add(v)`, `.has(v)`, `.delete(v)`, `.clear()`, `.keys(...ignored)`, `.values(...ignored)`, `.forEach((value, value2, set) => expr, thisArg?, ...ignored)`, `.size`; numeric values use SameValueZero semantics, ignored key/value iterator arguments are evaluated before being discarded, and `forEach` accepts inline expression-body or single-return block-body callbacks and named callback references. Optional `thisArg` values are evaluated once and bound for callbacks that declare `this: any`, and trailing ignored arguments are evaluated before iteration. Tests: `map_set`, `map_set_same_value_zero`, `set_keys`, `map_set_for_each`, `map_set_for_each_refs`, `map_set_for_each_this_arg`
- Direct `for...of` over values. Test: `map_set_for_of`
- `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)`. Test: `collection_object_methods`
- ES2025 set composition: `.union(other, ...ignored)`, `.intersection(other, ...ignored)`, `.difference(other, ...ignored)`, `.symmetricDifference(other, ...ignored)`, `.isSubsetOf(other, ...ignored)`, `.isSupersetOf(other, ...ignored)`, `.isDisjointFrom(other, ...ignored)`. The argument must be a `Set<T>` of the same element type; ignored trailing arguments are evaluated after the set operand; runtime helpers `tsc_set_union`/`tsc_set_intersection`/`tsc_set_difference`/`tsc_set_symmetric_difference`/`tsc_set_is_subset_of`/`tsc_set_is_superset_of`/`tsc_set_is_disjoint_from` honor SameValueZero element matching and insertion order for typed and dynamic `Set<any>` values. Tests: `set_composition`, `set_composition_ignored_arguments`

### `WeakMap<K, V>` / `WeakSet<T>`
- Typed object-key `WeakMap` supports `.set(k, v)`, `.get(k)`, `.has(k)`, `.delete(k)`, and construction from typed `Map<K, V>` or `ObjectEntry<V, K>[]` sources with matching object-key/value types. Dynamic `WeakMap<any, any>` supports nullish empty sources, boxed dynamic pair arrays, object-key validation for construction and `.set(...)`, and ES-compatible primitive-key `.get(...)` / `.has(...)` / `.delete(...)` results. Supported source constructor extras are evaluated and ignored. Tests: `weak_collections`, `weak_collections_dynamic`, `map_object_entry_constructors`, `collection_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- Typed object-key `WeakSet` supports `.add(v)`, `.has(v)`, `.delete(v)`, and construction from typed `T[]` arrays or matching `Set<T>` sources. Dynamic `WeakSet<any>` supports nullish empty sources, boxed dynamic array/string source validation, object-value validation for construction and `.add(...)`, and ES-compatible primitive-value `.has(...)` / `.delete(...)` results. Supported source constructor extras are evaluated and ignored. Tests: `weak_collections`, `weak_collections_dynamic`, `collection_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)` on both weak collections. Test: `collection_object_methods`
- Runtime storage reuses pointer-key map/set tables; there is no iteration API exposed.

### `WeakRef<T>`
- `new WeakRef(target, ...ignored)` creates a typed weak-reference wrapper after evaluating ignored trailing constructor arguments, and dynamic `WeakRef<any>` validates object targets at runtime. `.deref(...ignored)` returns `T | undefined` or the original dynamic value after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `weak_ref`, `weak_ref_dynamic`, `weak_ref_finalization_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)`. Tests: `collection_object_methods`, `weak_ref`
- Runtime storage is a small pointer wrapper.

### `FinalizationRegistry<T>`
- `new FinalizationRegistry<T>(cleanupCallback, ...ignored)` is constructible against any cleanup-callback signature; the callback value and ignored trailing constructor arguments are evaluated for side effects and discarded. Tests: `finalization_registry`, `weak_ref_finalization_constructor_ignored_arguments`
- `.register(target, heldValue, unregisterToken?, ...ignored)` evaluates target, held value, token, and ignored extras, treats explicit `undefined` unregister tokens as omitted, records the optional token entry, validates dynamic targets/tokens as objects, and `.unregister(unregisterToken, ...ignored)` removes any matching entries after evaluating ignored extras and dynamic token validation, returning whether anything was removed. Tests: `finalization_registry`, `finalization_registry_dynamic`
- `.toString(...ignored)` and `.toLocaleString(...ignored)` return `"[object FinalizationRegistry]"`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)` returns the receiver. Test: `finalization_registry`
- This AOT runtime has no GC-finalizer plumbing, so the cleanup callback is never invoked. The behavior matches WeakRef in spirit: type-correct API surface without observable garbage-collection callbacks.
