## 5. Strings

All methods on the `String` interface map to `tsc_str_*` runtime calls:

- `.length` → `tsc_str_length`
- `.charAt(i?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_char_at` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_char_code_at`
- `.charCodeAt(i?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_char_code_at`, returning JS UTF-16 code units after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_char_code_at`
- `.at(i?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_at`, including negative-index lookup after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `string_at`, `string_char_code_at`
- `.codePointAt(i?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_code_point_at` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `string_codepoints`, `string_char_code_at`
- `String.fromCharCode(...)` → `tsc_str_from_char_code_values`, consuming one dynamic argument collection. Test: `string_codepoints`
- `String.fromCodePoint(...)` → `tsc_str_from_code_point_values`, consuming the same argument representation and throwing catchable native `RangeError` for invalid code points. Tests: `string_from_code_point`, `string_from_code_point_errors`
- `String.raw` tagged templates concatenate raw segments with stringified substitutions, including dynamic substitution evaluation. Tests: `string_raw`, `string_raw_dynamic`
- `.indexOf(needle, position?, ...ignored)` / `.lastIndexOf(needle, position?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_index_of`, `tsc_str_last_index_of` after evaluating ignored extra arguments, including explicit `undefined` position defaults. Tests: `string_last_index_of`, `string_search_positions`
- `.localeCompare(other, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_locale_compare` using deterministic runtime string ordering after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_locale_compare`
- `.includes(needle, position?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_includes` after evaluating ignored extra arguments, including explicit `undefined` position defaults. Test: `string_search_positions`
- `.startsWith(p, position?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_starts_with` after evaluating ignored extra arguments, including explicit `undefined` position defaults. Test: `string_search_positions`
- `.endsWith(p, endPosition?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_ends_with` after evaluating ignored extra arguments, including explicit `undefined` end-position defaults. Test: `string_search_positions`
- `.slice(start?, end?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_slice`, including explicit `undefined` defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `strings`
- `.substring(start?, end?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_substring`, including clamp/swap semantics and explicit `undefined` defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_substring`
- `.substr(start?, length?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_substr`, including negative-start, length clamping semantics, and explicit `undefined` defaults after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_substr`
- `.toUpperCase(...ignored)` / `.toLowerCase(...ignored)` → `tsc_str_to_upper`, `tsc_str_to_lower` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `strings`
- `.toString(...ignored)` / `.toLocaleString(...ignored)` / `.valueOf(...ignored)` return the typed string receiver unchanged after evaluating ignored extra arguments, and inherited `hasOwnProperty(prop, ...ignored)` / `propertyIsEnumerable(prop, ...ignored)` report string indexes plus non-enumerable `length` ownership. Test: `string_object_methods`
- `.normalize(form?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_normalize` backed by ICU for NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, including explicit `undefined` default forms after evaluating ignored extra arguments, with catchable invalid-form validation. Tests: `string_normalize`, `string_normalize_errors`
- Typed strings participate in `Object.keys`, `Object.values`, `Object.entries`, `Object.getOwnPropertyNames`, `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(s)`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Reflect.get`, `Reflect.has`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `Reflect.deleteProperty`, and `Reflect.set` with read-only string index descriptors plus non-enumerable `length`. Test: `string_object_enumeration`
- `.trim(...ignored)` / `.trimStart(...ignored)` / `.trimEnd(...ignored)` plus `.trimLeft(...ignored)` / `.trimRight(...ignored)` aliases → `tsc_str_trim`, `tsc_str_trim_start`, `tsc_str_trim_end` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `string_trim_edges`, `string_trim_aliases`
- `.isWellFormed(...ignored)` / `.toWellFormed(...ignored)` → `true` / receiver identity for the runtime's validated UTF-8 string representation after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `string_well_formed`
- `.repeat(n, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_repeat` after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `strings`
- `.padStart(len, pad?, ...ignored)` / `.padEnd(len, pad?, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_pad_start`, `tsc_str_pad_end`, including explicit `undefined` default padding after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Test: `strings`
- `.replace(search, repl, ...ignored)` → `tsc_str_replace` or `tsc_str_replace_regex` (if `search` is a RegExp); string and RegExp replacement strings expand dollar, whole-match, prefix, and suffix tokens, and RegExp replacements also expand capture tokens after evaluating ignored extra arguments. Tests: `string_split_limit`, `strings`
- `.concat(...strings)` → repeated `tsc_str_concat`. Test: `string_concat`
- `for...of` over strings → `tsc_str_chars`, yielding one string per UTF-8 code point. Test: `string_for_of`
- String + anything → concat with automatic stringification
- Index access `s[i]` → same as `charAt`

Tests: `strings`, `string_at`, `string_concat`, `string_for_of`, `string_last_index_of`, `string_locale_compare`, `string_match_all`, `string_normalize`, `string_normalize_errors`, `string_object_methods`, `string_search_regex`, `string_split_limit`, `string_substr`, `string_substring`, `string_trim_edges`, `wordcount`

## 8. Error handling

- `throw expr` — stringifies `expr` and `longjmp`s to the nearest enclosing `try`. Test: `exceptions`
- `try { } catch (e) { } finally { }` — catch binding is `tsc_str_t* e = tsc_current_error()`
- `new Error(message?, options?, ...ignored)`, callable `Error(message?, options?, ...ignored)`, and the same constructor/callable forms for `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`, `URIError`, and `AggregateError` create a narrow Error object subset exposing `.name`, `.message`, `.cause`, `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, and `.valueOf(...ignored)`. Extra constructor and string/value method arguments are evaluated then ignored where JavaScript ignores them, explicit `undefined` message/options slots use JavaScript defaults without misrouting ignored extras into cause handling, literal and earlier static `const` `{ cause }` options are stored as dynamic values, `AggregateError` stores `.errors`, and throwing one of these errors still stringifies into the existing exception string channel. Error instances expose bounded non-enumerable `name`, `message`, `cause`, and `errors` fields through `Object.getOwnPropertyNames`, `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(s)`, `Object.hasOwn`, inherited `hasOwnProperty(prop, ...ignored)`, `Object.prototype.*.call(...)`, read-only `Object.isExtensible(...)` / `Object.isSealed(...)` / `Object.isFrozen(...)` checks, `Reflect.get`, `Reflect.has`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, and `Reflect.isExtensible(...)`, while `Object.keys` / `values` / `entries` and `propertyIsEnumerable(...)` stay empty/false. Tests: `error_instances`, `error_constructors`, `error_more_constructors`, `aggregate_error_constructor`, `error_cause`, `error_object_methods`, `suppressed_error`
- Nested try/catch with re-throw. Test: `exceptions`
- Uncaught exceptions print `Uncaught: <msg>` and exit 1
- Runtime: `tsc_try_push`, `tsc_try_pop`, `tsc_throw_str`, `tsc_rethrow`, `tsc_current_error` + `setjmp`/`longjmp`

## 9. JSON

- `JSON.stringify(value)` — type-driven, recurses into:
  - Primitives (number/string/boolean) with proper JSON escaping
  - Arrays → `[...]`
  - Class/interface values → `{"field":value,...}` using the declared property list from the TypeScript checker
- Runtime: `tsc_json_escape_string`, `tsc_json_num`. Test: `json`
- Top-level dynamic `JSON.stringify` now returns boxed `undefined` for `undefined`, functions, and callable proxies while retaining JSON `null` substitution for those values inside arrays and object-property omission for objects. Tests: `json_stringify_dynamic_top_level`, `proxy_callable_json`, `proxy_nested_callable_identity`, `proxy_revocable_identity`
- `JSON.parse(text)` returns a NaN-boxed dynamic `tsc_value_t`, with recursive parsing for objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null, including `\uXXXX` string escapes, surrogate-pair decoding to UTF-8, and catchable syntax failures. Tests: `dynamic_values`, `json_parse_errors`

## 9.5 Dynamic values

- `any` / `unknown` and heterogeneous unions map to `tsc_value_t`, a NaN-boxed `uint64_t` dynamic value.
- Dynamic values can hold numbers, strings, booleans, null, undefined, arrays, and object pointers.
- Dynamic array/object literals box heterogeneous fields/elements into `tsc_value_t`.
- Dynamic array literals typed as `any` support spread from dynamic arrays, dynamic/typed strings, and typed arrays, boxing spread elements into `tsc_value_t`. Test: `dynamic_array_spread`
- Dynamic property and element access supports object properties, array indices, and `.length` on dynamic arrays/strings.
- Dynamic property writes (`obj.x = value`, `obj["x"] = value`, numeric-key `obj[1.5]` / `obj[-1]` / `obj[4294967295]` / `obj[1e21]`) and compound/logical writes (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `**=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `>>>=`, `&&=`, `||=`, `??=`) lower through descriptor-aware `tsc_value_set_prop` / dynamic operator helpers with RHS short-circuiting for logical assignment. Tests: `dynamic_property_assignment`, `dynamic_property_logical_assign`, `dynamic_bitwise_ops`

### `util`
- `util.format(format?, ...args)` implements a bounded Node format helper. It supports `%s` (coerced to string), `%d` / `%i` (coerced to number and formatted as integer), `%f` (coerced to number and formatted as float), `%j` (coerced to JSON string), and `%%` (literal percent). ### `TextEncoder` / `TextDecoder`
- Global `TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder` constructors support deterministic UTF-8 encode and decode basics. `new TextEncoder().encode(string)` returns a UTF-8 encoded `Buffer` representing the string, or an empty `Buffer` if the input is omitted/undefined. `new TextDecoder(label?).decode(buffer)` decodes the UTF-8 `Buffer` back to a string, or returns an empty string if omitted/undefined, with catchable validation failures for unsupported encoding labels (only UTF-8 is supported). Test: `text_encoder_decoder`

- AOT closure diagnostics reject unknown-source `eval`, `Function` / `new Function`, non-finite `require(variable)` without a static proof or manifest, unallow-listed literal native addon specifiers ending in `.node`, and unallow-listed literal package imports/requires whose installed package root contains `build/Release/*.node`, package `exports` / `imports` references to `.node`, or package-private `#...` imports that resolve to `.node` or target external native-addon packages, including transitive imports from emitted package sources under `node_modules`. Constant runtime-code strings compile AOT for expression `eval("...")` and constant-body `Function("return ...")` / `new Function("return ...")` without enabling unsafe eval, including earlier local static `const` string aliases, single-valued template-literal type aliases, and `Function("arg", "return ...")` / `new Function("arg", "return ...")` forms when parameter-name strings are static, earlier local static `const` aliases, or single-valued template-literal type aliases. `--runtime-code-manifest <path>` is an explicit compile-time allow-list for non-constant runtime-code source strings; manifest entries use JSON shape `{ "eval": ["1 + 2"], "functions": ["return 42;"] }` or named object maps such as `{ "eval": { "sum": "1 + 2" }, "functions": { "answer": "return 42;" } }`, dispatch over the finite string set at runtime, and lower matching entries to generated AOT constants rather than dynamically loading code; manifest-backed `Function(...)` dispatch uses the final function-body argument and requires preceding parameter-name strings to be static. Top-level finite const string `require(name)` specifiers, including bound `require` forms, string concatenation, template expressions whose parts are all statically known, conditional alternatives, identifiers annotated as inline or type-aliased string-literal unions or finite template-literal string types, top-level const string maps/arrays used through element/property access, statically computed map keys, static `path.basename(...)` / `path.dirname(...)` / `path.extname(...)` fragments from `path` / `node:path` bindings, static `querystring.escape(...)` / `querystring.unescape(...)` fragments from `querystring` / `node:querystring` bindings, static `util.format(...)` string fragments from `util` / `node:util` bindings, and typed `require.call(module, spec)` / `require.apply(module, args)` / `module.require.call(module, spec)` / `module.require.apply(module, args)` / module-alias `mod.require.call/apply(mod, ...)` / `Reflect.apply(require | module.require | moduleAlias.require | requireAlias, moduleAlias, args)` wrapper forms with inline or earlier static one-element argument tuples, are resolved into the AOT module graph. Side-effect-only `require(name)` statements include every possible specifier as an eager AOT module edge; value-returning finite-set `require(name)` calls dispatch over the same finite alternatives for AOT-known `module.exports = ...` values and materialize AOT-known `module.exports.name = ...` named exports plus object-literal named exports with package-local `require(...)` spreads into dynamic objects. `--dynamic-require-manifest <path>` is an explicit compile-time allow-list for non-finite dynamic require sites; manifest entries use JSON shape `{ "requires": ["./specifier"] }` or a named object map such as `{ "requires": { "primary": "./specifier" } }`, enter the AOT module graph, and share the same runtime finite dispatch. `--unsafe-eval` is an explicit compile-time gate for runtime code compilation that remains available for unknown runtime source strings: it emits embedded Node bridge calls for `eval` and callable `Function` values, compiles those exported bridge entry points behind `TSC_UNSAFE_EVAL`, copies `runtime/tsc_node_embed.cc`, forwards dynamic `Function` invocation arguments into V8, and requires discoverable `libnode` inputs when linking. `--native-addon-manifest <path>` is a separate compile-time allow-list for known native addons; manifest entries map literal specifiers to concrete `.node` files, lower to `tsc_node_native_addon(...)`, copy `runtime/tsc_node_embed.cc`, and require discoverable `libnode` inputs when linking without enabling the unsafe eval/Function entry points. Direct `.node` default imports and `import { default as value }` bindings are declared as `any` for manifest-backed native bridge imports, and manifest-backed `require(...)` destructuring reads named properties, applies default initializers for `undefined` bridge properties, or materializes rest objects from the embedded Node bridge value. The embedded bridge initializes a Node environment, captures `require` for manifest-backed native-addon loads, and maps V8 object own properties into dynamic `tsc_value_t` objects. - `--emit-c-only` — skip gcc, just write the generated `main.c` for inspection.
- `--keep-build-dir <path>` — keep intermediate files rather than using a tempdir.
- `--verbose` — print compile steps + the full gcc command line.
- `--no-gc` — link without Boehm GC (leaking `calloc` fallback) for environments where `libgc-dev` isn't installed.
- `--release` — link a smaller release binary using gcc `-Os -s` instead of the default `-O2`; on Linux, release builds also compile with `-ffunction-sections` / `-fdata-sections` and link with `-Wl,--gc-sections`. Test: `release_build`
- `TSC2C_CC` / `TSC2C_CXX` — override the C and C++ compiler commands used by the linker driver; Linux CI runs both gcc and clang lanes.
- `--unsafe-eval` — opt into runtime code compilation through the embedded Node bridge and compile the unsafe bridge entry points behind `TSC_UNSAFE_EVAL`. Linking requires `libnode`; set `TSC2C_LIBNODE` and optionally `TSC2C_NODE_INCLUDE` when Node headers/libs are not in the active Node prefix.
- `--native-addon-manifest <path>` — opt specific native addon specifiers into the embedded Node bridge without enabling unsafe eval/Function entry points. The JSON shape is `{ "addons": { "specifier": "relative/or/absolute/addon.node" } }`; paths are resolved relative to the manifest and must point to existing `.node` files.
- Embedded Node native-addon and unsafe-eval bridge values preserve function-valued properties in both directions: V8 functions retain their name, arity, and constructor capability when converted to generic or non-constructable closure `tsc_value_t` identities, and compiled AOT function values passed back into V8 are exposed as V8 callbacks.
- C++ runtime sources compile as C++20, retaining Node 18/22 header compatibility while satisfying the C++20 requirement in Node 26 V8 headers.
- `--dynamic-require-manifest <path>` — opt non-finite dynamic require sites into finite AOT dispatch. The JSON shape is `{ "requires": ["./specifier"] }`, a named object map such as `{ "requires": { "primary": "./specifier" } }`, or caller-scoped maps such as `{ "requires": { "src/loader.ts": ["./specifier"] } }`; non-object top-level JSON values are rejected before reading `requires`, caller-scoped entries match exact normalized absolute source-file paths, caller-scoped entries only allow dynamic requires in matching source files, and unmatched callers remain rejected. Tests: `dynamic_require_manifest_by_file`, `dynamic_require_manifest_by_file_unmatched`, `dynamic_require_manifest_by_file_exact`, `dynamic_require_manifest_invalid_root`
- `--runtime-code-manifest <path>` — opt non-constant `eval(...)` / `Function(...)` source strings into finite AOT dispatch without enabling unsafe eval. The JSON shape is `{ "eval": ["1 + 2"], "functions": ["return 42;"] }` or named object maps such as `{ "eval": { "sum": "1 + 2" }, "functions": { "answer": "return 42;" } }`; each listed source string must parse as a supported AOT constant expression or constant-return function body.
- OpenSSL (`libssl-dev`), ICU (`libicu-dev`), and GMP (`libgmp-dev`) are linked for crypto hashing, Unicode normalization, and BigInt.
- Shortest round-trip number formatting — `tsc_str_from_num` probes `%.*g` with precision 1..17 until the formatted value strtods back to the original. Matches JS's `Number.prototype.toString` output on common cases.
- Multi-pass emission (struct fwd-decls → struct bodies → function/method protos → function/method bodies → module init bodies → main) so cycles and forward references work cleanly.

- Direct branch `return await` now carries an assigned-before-use uninitialized `var` through an await-free `while` prelude across async declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now carries assigned-before-use uninitialized `var` state through await-free `while`, `do while`, ordinary `for`, `for-of`, and `for-in` preludes across async declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now hoists simple `var` declarations inside all five await-free loop-prelude body shapes, preserves their assignments through the suspension, and retains JavaScript `undefined` on the `while` false fallthrough across async declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now hoists a simple `var` declared in an await-free caught `try` / `catch` / `finally` prelude and preserves the caught assignment across declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now hoists simple escaping `var` declarations from await-free `if`, `switch`, and normal `try`/`finally` preludes, preserving selected and fallthrough values across async declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now supports one optional awaited expression statement in an `if` arm, with an await-free `else` arm, before the final await and preserves exact branch scheduling across async declarations, class methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now preserves an initialized local assigned by the awaited or synchronous arm of that optional `if` shape before the final await across declarations, methods, and function values. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Direct branch `return await` now also preserves typed primitive and top-level dynamic `any` uninitialized locals assigned by either arm of that optional `if` shape before the final await, including undefined fallthrough when the optional arm is not entered, and supports an await-free nested `if` prelude inside the awaited arm; nested dynamic captures and awaited nested control flow remain deferred. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Leading awaited-local chains now hoist nested dynamic `var` captures declared by await-free `if` preludes across async declarations, methods, and function values, including undefined fallthrough. Test: `async_await_while_condition`.
- Dispatch task adapters now preserve typed ArrayBuffer, DataView, TextEncoder, and TextDecoder results across threaded and serial backends with checked runtime boxing/unboxing. Tests: `dispatch_binary_types`, `dispatch_serial_binary_types`.
- Async expression sequences now have a typed planner IR with explicit suspension-state IDs and next/short-circuit edges, separated from C emission. The shared arbitrary-length plan handles awaited spread operands in calls, constructors, array literals, and object literals while preserving left-to-right ordering and captured prelude locals. Test: `async_await_expression_sequence_spread`.
- Leading async return plans now record prelude-owned parameters separately from true outer captures. Nested loop adapters evaluate the prelude in their callback scope, then transfer its live locals into the subsequent await stages without attempting to initialize those locals at function entry. Test: `async_await_loop_leading_prelude_capture`.
- Awaited logical loop conditions now lower from a typed control-flow graph whose state edges distinguish truthy, falsy, and nullish results. One collection-based emitter handles two-state, conditional, homogeneous, mixed, and deeper nested graphs, replacing the former first/second emitter, three-await conditional emitter, and hard-coded association catalog. Test: `async_await_loop_condition_graph`.
- Static import and re-export attribute clauses now accept every ECMAScript line terminator before `with` through one equal-width scanner worklist. Parser normalization preserves exposed source bytes, line maps, and node offsets, covers whitespace/comment trivia across every declaration form, and leaves dynamic import plus legacy `assert` untouched; the minimal standard-library surface now declares string-valued `ImportAttributes`. Property/stress: `tests/property/module-linking.property.test.ts`; native regression: `import_attributes_line_terminator`.
- Script `var` declaration instantiation now follows one source-ancestor scope walk instead of accepting only direct source-file variable statements. Arbitrarily nested simple-name declarations and `for`/`for-in`/`for-of` heads share the canonical global-object binding, while function, class, static-block, and module boundaries remain local. Property/stress: `tests/property/script-global-binding.property.test.ts`; native host regression: `tests/test262/self.test.ts`.
- Native module resolution now includes attested `.json` resources, validates strict JSON through one explicit container-frame worklist, and creates a default-only synthetic Module Record. The pinned invalid-source and named-binding negatives now fail for their specified resolution causes instead of an absent-resource fallback. Properties: `tests/property/json-syntax.property.test.ts`, `tests/property/module-linking.property.test.ts`.
- One-argument runtime `JSON.parse` now recognizes exact JSON whitespace/string/number/container grammar and materializes values through one explicit root/array/object frame worklist instead of recursive C calls. Malformed inputs throw `SyntaxError`; escaped lone surrogates are retained; duplicate object keys take the last value; and `"__proto__"` is defined as an ordinary own data property. DCE only removes a statically known parse after the shared strict validator proves that it cannot throw. Property: `tests/property/json-parse-materialization.property.test.ts`; native regressions: `json_parse_errors`, `json_parse_deep_worklist` in both memory modes.
- Static JSON Modules now enter the compiler graph as JSON source records and evaluate once into one GC-rooted exporter-owned default slot. Direct default imports, `import { default as ... }`, and namespace imports share value identity; the namespace contains exactly `default`, uses the existing null-prototype/non-extensible exotic representation, and preserves mutations to object/array roots. Property: `tests/property/json-module.property.test.ts`; native regression: `json_module_default` in both memory modes.
- Static imports and re-exports now derive one canonical ECMA-262 ModuleRequest Record from their specifier and decoded, UTF-16-key-sorted attribute collection. Request equality and graph deduplication are independent of declaration/attribute count and source order; escaped duplicate keys fail as an early `SyntaxError`, unsupported keys fail during resolution, and the host's `type: "javascript"` / `type: "json"` policy is shared by the ordinary compiler and native Test262 linker. Property/stress: `tests/property/module-linking.property.test.ts`; negative native regression: `module_request_resolution_diagnostic`; implementation: `src/module-request.ts`.
- Finite-AOT dynamic import keeps one canonical target-specifier collection without turning lazy targets into startup edges. One source-tree worklist discovers ImportCalls, cardinality-independent finite alternatives enter the native program, and one dependency-graph worklist initializes the selected target in a queued Promise job. ImportCall options are no longer a compile-time object-literal shape: both argument expressions evaluate once in source order, then one ordinary object/Proxy enumeration path collects runtime `with` attributes, preserves abrupt-value identity, rejects invalid options/values/host keys with `TypeError`, and enforces JavaScript/JSON resource matching. Per-module evaluation state preserves one-time execution, namespace identity, and cached abrupt completion. Runtime Promise handlers accept boxed callable values such as Test262 `$DONE` and ignore boxed non-callables as required. Property/stress: `tests/property/dynamic-import.property.test.ts`; pinned diagnostic slices cover option getters, enumeration, abrupt values, logical-operand preservation, JSON selection, and trailing commas; native regressions: `dynamic_import_aot`, `dynamic_import_nonfinite_diagnostic`; declaration: `stdlib/lib.core.d.ts`.
- The native Test262 profile now earns structured negative-phase classification. Parser and contextual early errors are emitted as `parse`, dependency syntax/linking failures as `resolution`, and generated-native throws as `runtime`, each with a source origin and exact constructor. Contextual control-flow validation now traverses one explicit `(node, context)` worklist, resets at function boundaries, preserves source order, and remains stack-independent for deeply nested ASTs. Property/stress: `tests/property/test262-negative-phase.property.test.ts`; protocol/native integration: `tests/test262/self.test.ts`.
- Promise combinator intake now routes boxed untyped-JavaScript array values through the same dynamic iterable materializer used by `any[]`, rather than rejecting the compiler's canonical `T_VALUE` representation before `Promise.all` / `race` / `any` / `allSettled` can normalize their elements. The dynamic-import property probe exercises the boxed path natively in both memory modes, and the pinned ImportCall primitive-option partitions now reach and pass their intended runtime assertions.
- Arbitrary Symbol PropertyKeys now use one opaque identity-bearing carrier shared by ordinary objects, arrays, functions, computed operations, Reflect, Proxy traps/invariants, descriptor maps, `Object.assign`, and own-key projections. This replaces well-known-name sentinels, preserves same-description identity and String collision freedom, and keeps String/Symbol partitions in canonical `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` order. Property/stress: `tests/property/symbol-coercion.property.test.ts`; pinned diagnostic: dynamic-import attribute enumeration in strict and sloppy modes; native regressions cover Proxy ownKeys, descriptors, symbols, invariants, and copy ordering.
- Finite `$262.evalScript` discovery now visits the complete TypeScript AST through one explicit child worklist; callback return values can no longer truncate sibling traversal, while nested and branched static-source alternatives still enter the same transitive exact-source graph. At emitter boundaries, top-level binder-isolated Script `this` is classified from its runtime Global Environment semantics instead of the external-module checker artifact, so `Object` integrity and descriptor operations receive the actual global object. The generated property specification exercises sibling/transitive discovery, the real harness's bound primordials, global-object descriptors, non-extensibility, and repeated evaluation in both memory modes. The pinned `script-decl-var` strict/sloppy diagnostic scenarios now execute natively; the targeted result remains non-claimable.
- Reusable Script evaluators now return the actual ScriptEvaluation result instead of unconditional `undefined`. One rooted UpdateEmpty slot follows the emitted statement tree, prevents otherwise-prunable expression values from disappearing, preserves earlier values across empty declarations and non-entered branches, and carries loop/labeled/block results without statement-shape dispatch. Structured try emission snapshots the enclosing completion, discards partial values on a caught abrupt path, and restores the try/catch result after a normally completing `finally`. The dual-memory property specification derives the normal/empty/caught/finally identity partitions and sends one representative deeply nested statement tree through the same slot; neither the partition inventory nor stress depth is completion evidence.
